doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Philadelphia and the move to New York
title: Carmen McRae, Jo Jones and the move to New York
summary: He toured with McRae, led a trio with Jo Jones, then moved to New York around 1959.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did it come to a point where you felt you needed to go to New York? What prompted the move to New York?

Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. I was in Philadelphia and Carmen McRae came to town without a piano player, and I went and filled in with her. And when she left I left with her. I was with her for maybe two years and I came back to Philadelphia, and then Jo Jones, of Count Basie fame, Jo Jones the drummer, he decided that he wanted to have a trio and he called me and I did that for a year, still based in Philadelphia. Then I got back from the thing with Jo Jones and I said I’m working only with people from New York and I know that’s where I want to be, so why shouldn’t I go there. So I did.
